business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - DTC Brand Webstore

stage_1.expense_line_item: Minimum share capital €12,000 (not an expense; funds deposited with notary and transferred to company's blocked bank account after incorporation)
stage_1.legal_fee_basis: Statutory paid-up capital requirement for SARL

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales, as amended, particularly Articles 710-1 to 710-24 (SARL); Luxembourg law on commercial companies and the law of 19 May 2023 on the digitalization of the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Authentic deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) and articles of association (statuts), filed electronically via LBR e-filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid up at incorporation. Funds must be deposited in a blocked escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution or held by the notary, with a blocked-funds certificate (blocage de fonds) issued to the notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDER OF LUXEMBOURG SARL. (1) The subscriber approves the draft Articles of Association and subscribes to all 12,000 ordinary shares of EUR 1.00 each, representing the full paid-up capital. (2) The registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. (3) The sole manager (Gérant) is appointed for an indefinite term, with sole signature authority. (4) The manager is authorised to open bank accounts, instruct the notary to effect payment of subscription funds from the escrow account, and complete registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register. (5) All necessary statutory declarations are made and delegated to the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Notary and Corporate Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary in the chosen judicial arrondissement and LBR online corporate name search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary, execute the engagement letter, provide KYC/AML documents for all shareholders and managers, and conduct a formal name availability search on the LBR portal. Instruct the notary to reserve the exact corporate name, if necessary, and prepare the draft articles of association in accordance with Articles 710-1 et seq.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of each shareholder and manager
Proof of residence not older than 3 months
Reference letter from a bank
Draft Articles of Association
Name reservation confirmation (if obtained)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the corporate name is rejected, submit an alternative name via the notary within 1 business day; if KYC files are insufficient, provide supplemental residence or source-of-funds evidence within 48 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Capital Deposit in Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) or notary's escrow client account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional bank account in the name of the company 'in formation' and deposit the full EUR 12,000 share capital. Instruct the bank to issue a blocked-funds certificate (blocage de fonds) addressed to the notary, or alternatively deposit the funds in the notary's escrow account under the company's name. The capital must remain blocked until the deed is signed.
required_dossiers: Provisional bank account opening application
AML/KYC questionnaires for shareholders and managers
Identification documents and corporate profile
Source of funds declaration and bank statements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises a supplemental information request, provide signed source-of-funds declarations and recent bank statements within 48 hours; if the bank refuses, switch to the notary's escrow facility without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend before the notary for signature of the authentic deed of incorporation. The notary verifies the subscribers' identity, legal capacity, blocked capital certificate, and compliance with the SARL provisions of the law of 10 August 1915. The deed incorporates the full articles of association and must be signed by all subscribers and the notary.
required_dossiers: Draft notarial deed prepared by the notary
Blocked-funds certificate or notary escrow confirmation
Name reservation confirmation
Full KYC/AML file of shareholders and managers
Approved Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies omissions or drafting errors, execute a rectification side-letter on the spot; if legal capacity issues arise, provide notarized powers of attorney or additional corporate authorizations within 24 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the executed notarial deed and statutory information electronically via the LBR e-filing portal within 5 business days of signature. The filing includes legal entity identity, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, managers' details, and confirmation of capital paid up. Pay the statutory registration fee online.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation (digital sealed file)
LBR e-filing form (Acte constitutif et statuts)
Power of attorney for the notary (if required)
Proof of fee payment (bank receipt or portal transaction)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (observation), submit a corrected filing or supplementary documents through the same e-filing portal within 15 days; if the filing is rejected for technical reasons, re-submit a corrected XML/PDF package and contact the LBR helpline for expedited review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in Official Gazette and RCS Extract Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the RCS publishes the incorporation notice in the official electronic gazette. Once the publication is confirmed, obtain the official RCS extract (extrait d'inscription) and the registration number, which evidences the legal existence of the SARL and permits subsequent tax and social registrations.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
RCS extract (extrait d'inscription)
Notary filing receipt
Bank blocked-funds release confirmation (post-registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is delayed, contact LBR with the filing receipt and request expedited publication. If the extract contains inaccuracies, file a request for rectification via the notary within 2 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure online DTC retail; for any physical warehouse or logistics activity, the competent authority is the Ministry of the Economy, Directorate for Industry (Direction de l'industrie).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) is required for a non-physical e-commerce store under Luxembourg law; registration with the RCS suffices.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for pure internet retail with no production or physical site; a simple declaration may be required only if a warehouse or logistics facility with mechanical ventilation or waste storage exceeds environmental thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for virtual operations. If warehousing is added, compliance with Luxembourg waste law (packaging waste, WEEE), EU REACH Article 33 supply-chain obligations, and VOC/odor limits for any light industrial activity would apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety certificate is required for a pure online store without physical premises. If an office or warehouse is used, a fire safety conformity certificate from the Luxembourg Fire and Rescue Service (SIS) and a building occupancy certificate are required; if employees are present, a workplace clearance under Labor and Mines Inspectorate (ITM) rules must be obtained.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes (corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT registration and compliance; Administration des douanes et accises (Luxembourg Customs) for export/customs procedures. Electronic portals: eCDF (ecdf.etat.lu) for VAT and customs filings, impotsdirects.public.lu for direct tax formalities, and MyGuichet.lu / Guichet.lu for corporate administrative procedures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the notarized incorporation deed for the SARL and file it with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS); the RCS/Luxembourg Business Registers issue the company registration number and automatically attribute the national identification number (matricule / n° d'identification national). Step 2: Submit the VAT registration application (Demande d'immatriculation à la TVA) to the AEDT via the eCDF online portal or the approved form within 15 days of the first taxable transaction; the AEDT allocates the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format: LU followed by 8 digits). Step 3: Direct tax registration (corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax) is effected automatically by the ACD based on the RCS file, using the national matricule as the taxpayer reference. Step 4: For cross-border e-commerce distance sales to non-taxable persons in other EU member states, optionally register for the Luxembourg One-Stop-Shop (OSS) scheme; update PSP accounts (Shopify Payments, PayPal, Stripe) with the allocated VAT ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the SARL is an opaque, non-transparent legal entity subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune). A resident SARL is taxed on worldwide income; no pass-through treatment is available; profits are not taxable at shareholder level until distributed, subject to dividend withholding tax and the participation exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; entity classification is statutory. Available elections and options: (i) opt into normal VAT taxation instead of the EUR 35,000 small-business exemption (Article 57 of the VAT Law); (ii) elect VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the VAT Law; (iii) elect Luxembourg fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) for corporate income tax and municipal business tax where a resident parent holds 95% or more directly or indirectly (Article 164bis LIR); (iv) elect the IP box regime (Article 50bis LIR) for qualifying IP income (80% exemption); (v) elect the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) for distance sales of goods to consumers in other EU member states; (vi) rely on the participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains. ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules are statutorily transposed and are non-elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, and EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a Luxembourg-established taxable person (SARL), VAT registration is required when carrying out taxable transactions, unless the statutory small-business exemption applies; the exemption is available where annual turnover (exclusive of VAT) does not exceed EUR 35,000 (Article 57 of the VAT Law). Once turnover exceeds EUR 35,000 or the entity opts to charge VAT, standard registration is mandatory. Separately, for distance sales of goods to non-taxable consumers in other EU member states, the EUR 10,000 Union-wide annual threshold governs the place of supply: below EUR 10,000, Luxembourg VAT applies; above EUR 10,000, the destination member state's VAT applies and must be reported through the OSS scheme unless a local VAT registration is held.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg imposes no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no government e-invoicing API clearance and no digital stamping regime for domestic invoices. Invoices must satisfy Articles 24-33 of the VAT Law, ensuring authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility. Electronic invoicing in accepted structured formats (PEPPOL/UBL, Factur-X, EDI, PDF-XML) is permitted. VAT returns and recapitulative statements of intra-Community supplies must be filed electronically through the eCDF portal. Luxembourg Customs and the AEDT apply risk-based data analysis for export controls. Mandatory e-invoicing and digital reporting obligations are expected to follow the EU ViDA package; until then, structured e-invoicing is recommended to substantiate export zero-rating and to future-proof DTC e-commerce records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Luxembourg to a destination outside the EU qualify for the 0% VAT rate under the provisions of the Luxembourg VAT Law transposing Article 146 of EU Directive 2006/112/EC, provided the goods are physically dispatched or transported out of the EU by the supplier, by the customer or by a third party acting on behalf of either, and the supplier obtains and retains genuine documentary proof of export. For DTC e-commerce (Shopify webstore), every parcel to a non-EU delivery address must be linked to a valid electronic export declaration with Movement Reference Number (MRN), transport documents and payment evidence; shipments to consumers in other EU member states are not zero-rated exports but distance sales taxable at destination via OSS. International services directly linked to exported goods (including transport and ancillary handling services) may also be zero-rated under the same evidentiary conditions. Export evidence must be completed within the period prescribed by the Luxembourg VAT administration, generally 90 days from the supply, and retained for audit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated Customs Export Declaration (electronic export declaration lodged via eCDF / Luxembourg Customs, bearing the MRN confirming physical exit from the EU customs territory)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR transport document (or integrated courier parcel manifest for DHL/FedEx/UPS) evidencing delivery to a non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (or SWIFT MT103 statement / PSP settlement report) evidencing receipt of the export price and FX repatriation
Commercial invoice and packing list (goods description, quantity, unit value, Incoterms and destination country)
Proof of customer identity and non-EU establishment (delivery address, purchase order, payment source and IP address evidence where available)
Export Summary Declaration / Exit Summary Declaration data and, where applicable, customs transit documentation for goods moving through other EU member states before exit
For intra-Community zero-rated supplies: the customer's valid EU VAT number and a timely recapitulative statement (Recap)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg Customs conduct risk-based audits of export zero-rating claims, cross-referencing eCDF declarations, carrier manifests, PSP settlement records and bank remittance certificates. Where the prescribed export evidence is missing, inconsistent or fabricated, the AEDT reassesses the supply at the applicable Luxembourg VAT rate and issues a deficiency assessment for the VAT not collected; default interest runs from the date the tax should have been paid. Administrative penalties include fines of up to EUR 250,000, and for willful tax evasion up to 200% of the evaded tax; the taxpayer may lose the right to deduct input VAT, be required to repay any export VAT refund previously granted, and may face joint and several liability for persons preparing or using fraudulent documentation. Criminal prosecution for tax fraud (fraude fiscale) may result in imprisonment of up to five years. The statutory reassessment period is generally three years from the end of the year in which the chargeable event arose; it may be extended in cases of fraud or material irregularities, and retroactive clawbacks may be accompanied by interest, penalties and publication of sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem and the European Central Bank framework for monetary policy; exchange control liberalization is governed by the Loi du 24 décembre 1988 concernant les relations financières avec l'étranger and the accompanying Grand-Ducal Regulation of 27 November 1989. The Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises credit institutions and enforces AML/CFT obligations (Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The EUR is a fully convertible reserve currency. Luxembourg has abolished exchange controls: current-account operations (e-commerce goods/services export proceeds) and capital-account operations (equity injections, shareholder loans, dividends, loan repayments) are unrestricted under Article 63 TFEU and the 1988 financial-relations law. No prior authorization or licence applies to a SARL operating an internet retail business. Profit remittance: dividends to an EU/EEA parent are exempt from Luxembourg withholding tax under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; dividends to third-country shareholders attract a 15% statutory withholding tax, reduced to 0–5% under applicable double-tax treaties. There is no foreign-exchange repatriation hurdle. The only practical compliance burden is balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the BCL, carried out by the resident credit institution on behalf of the SARL.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, conversion ratio, or repatriation deadline applies to export proceeds or internet-sale receipts. The mandatory conversion ratio is 0%; the SARL may retain foreign currency in EUR-denominated or USD/GBP/CAD/AUD multi-currency operating sub-accounts at the resident bank. The only legal duty is statistical: cross-border receipts and payments are reported by the resident credit institution to the BCL under BCL Regulation 2002/111 (balance-of-payments statistics, as amended) pursuant to ECB methodology. The SARL must identify the commercial purpose ('e-commerce sale of goods') in each payment instruction and provide settlement documentation to its bank for classification. A direct-reporting obligation to the BCL arises only if the company elects self-reporting or exceeds the materiality thresholds set by the BCL for direct statistical reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) and Operational Account (compte courant)
Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) and Operational Account with multi-currency sub-accounts
Operational Account (EUR and foreign-currency operating accounts)
Operational Account and Corporate Transaction Banking cash-management structure

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as a primary treasury rail, High as an auxiliary disbursement rail. An EU-licensed Electronic Money Institution (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business, or a Luxembourg-licensed EMI such as Monavate) may passport its licence into Luxembourg under PSD2 / Directive 2009/110/EC and provide multi-currency IBANs, fast FX, and virtual accounts without obtaining a Luxembourg banking licence. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI cannot grant credit or accept deposits repayable on demand, so surplus cash is not protected by the Luxembourg deposit-guarantee scheme (DGDL/DGS up to EUR 100,000 applies only to credit institutions); (ii) EMI client funds are safeguarded rather than deposit-insured; (iii) certain tier-1 banks and the Shopify payout regime require settlement into a regulated credit-institution account; (iv) the SARL remains responsible for the provenance-of-funds evidence accepted by the EMI as well as by its main bank. Recommended structure: keep the escrow and operating accounts at a CSSF-licensed bank and use EMIs only for low-value multi-currency supplier disbursements and FX conversion, with daily sweeping controls.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted under Luxembourg law when the bank applies the digital-identification framework (Law of 25 March 2020 as extended, read together with the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02). Bank policy in practice: (i) EU/EEA-resident directors and beneficial owners may complete video identification with an eIDAS-qualified electronic identity or a supervised live video session; (ii) non-EU residents are generally required to appear physically at a branch or to deliver certified true passport copies bearing an apostille and notarial certification; (iii) account-opening mandates and capital-escrow instructions may be executed with CSSF-accepted qualified electronic signatures, but BCEE, BIL, and Raiffeisen reserve the right to require an in-person interview of the ultimate beneficial owner when the ownership chain is non-European. A single physical visit by the directing shareholder or the appointed authorized signatory should be assumed in the onboarding workplan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face e-commerce merchant with global B2C counterparties, online-only contracts, and revenue collected via Shopify Payments, PayPal, and Stripe aggregators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized incorporation deed and articles of association (statuts); current RCS extract; RBE extract from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners; completed business-risk questionnaire mapping ISIC 4791 to the low-risk standard category; 12-month Shopify settlement dossier (transaction history, monthly payouts, refund and chargeback rates); published privacy policy, terms of sale, and return/refund policy; PCI-DSS attestation of compliance; SSL certificate and website domain evidence; statement of accepted payment methods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value inbound flows from three separate payment aggregators producing commingled or netted settlements with periodic cross-currency conversion entries in USD, GBP, CAD, and AUD.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-way reconciliation pack: Stripe, PayPal, and Shopify payout reports aligned with bank statements; documented weekly cash-reconciliation policy; explanation of netting, PSP fees, and multi-currency conversion entries; treasury ledger with traceable settlement-to-invoice mapping; refund policy and chargeback dashboard demonstrating a chargeback ratio below 1%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or indirect beneficial-ownership chain with the foreign parent ultimately owning the Luxembourg SARL, categorized as higher risk under CSSF Regulation 12-02.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate structure chart traced to ultimate natural persons; passport copies and proof of address for all beneficial owners; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence for the minimum capital injection; PEP-status declarations from all UBOs; notarized certificate of incumbency for the foreign parent; reference letter from the parent's existing bank where available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and geographical-risk signals arising from shipment to customers or suppliers in high-risk third countries, or a concern about unlicensed export activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Denied-party and sanctions-screening logs (EU consolidated list, OFAC, UN); IP-geoblocking statement confirming no webstore sales into sanctioned jurisdictions; trade-compliance attestation confirming no dual-use goods under Regulation (EU) 2021/821; pro-forma invoices, Incoterms evidence, transport documents, and customs declarations for goods entering the EU; supplier due-diligence file for inventory and fulfilment partners; annual trade-compliance certification to the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For incorporation: open a blocked 'compte bloqué' at a Luxembourg credit institution before notarization and transfer at least EUR 12,000 (the classic statutory minimum under Article 710-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915; if the company elects the reduced-capital regime introduced by the SARL modernization Law of 3 May 2024, the minimum may be as low as EUR 1 subject to the statutory balance-sheet restrictions) via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's bank. Remittance field 70 must state 'CAPITAL INJECTION – EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION – LU SARL'; where the bank's e-banking portal requests a purpose code, select the BCL/ECB balance-of-payments direct-investment equity category ('creation of enterprise'). The bank issues the attestation de blocage to the notary; funds are released to the operational account only after notarization and RCS registration. For post-incorporation working capital: inject through a documented shareholder loan (advance d'actionnaire) via SEPA Credit Transfer or MT103 with narrative 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN – LU SARL', supported by a signed loan agreement containing subordination language. CSSF KYC requires source-of-funds evidence for every inbound transfer of EUR 10,000 or more, including bank statements, tax returns, or liquidation documentation from the remitting party.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Open-account supplier payments: SWIFT MT103 (GPI-tracked) via the Luxembourg bank's correspondent network for non-euro jurisdictions; SEPA Credit Transfer and TARGET2 for Eurozone suppliers; SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for urgent low-value payments. High-value one-off inventory purchases requiring bank security: irrevocable commercial Letter of Credit via MT700 (at sight or deferred payment) with MT710/MT720 amendments, or documentary collections (MT400/MT410) where agreed. Platform and fulfilment costs: commercial card rails (Visa/Mastercard) for Google, Meta, and Shopify subscription fees; ACH and US Fedwire for US 3PL warehouses; GBP/CAD/AUD payments executed from the bank's multi-currency sub-accounts to avoid conversion spread. Retail-customer refunds are disbursed directly from the PSP wallet (PayPal, Stripe, Shopify Payments) and mirrored in treasury records; the corporate account does not execute B2C micro-wires except in extraordinary, fully documented cases.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CAD, and EUR/AUD FX forwards with tenors up to 12 months under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement / 1998 FX Definitions or the bank's master FX agreement; EMIR reporting applies as a non-financial counterparty (NFC-) below the clearing threshold.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNH or EUR/CNH for mainland-China inventory payables invoiced in renminbi, settled in EUR or USD only where the counterparty bank supports offshore-coverage; permitted without delivery of the underlying currency.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD CCS) to hedge a foreign-currency shareholder loan or long-dated working-capital exposure, with EUR collateral under a 1995/2006 ISDA Credit Support Annex.
European-style FX options and zero-cost collars (risk reversals) to protect a 12-month budgeted conversion rate while preserving upside on favourable currency movements.

Natural-hedging overlays: monthly matching of USD inflows from Shopify multi-currency settlements against USD supplier disbursements, with residual exposure converted to EUR on a rolling basis without any derivative documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts approval by the SARL shareholders' general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General meeting minutes retained in the corporate minute book; no regulatory filing at this step
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or approve annual accounts exposes the gérant to civil liability and delays the mandatory RCS filing; prolonged default risks court-ordered filing and judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of the approved annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes) with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after approval; for a calendar-year SARL, practically no later than 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to approximately EUR 5,000, court-ordered daily penalties (astreinte), and risk of administrative or judicial strike-off for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual direct tax declarations: corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC), and net wealth tax (ISF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) / Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: E-file no later than 31 December of the year following the tax period; calendar-year SARL: by 31 December of the next year, unless extension granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing can trigger taxation d'office (estimated assessment), default interest, late-filing penalties, and administrative collection measures; repeated failure to file may expose managers to criminal fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (UBO) in the Luxembourg beneficial-ownership register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) / Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March following the reporting year; any share transfer changing beneficial ownership must be filed within 1 month of the effective transfer date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or confirm UBO data is punishable by administrative fines and, in serious cases, criminal liability; inaccurate entries expose managers and shareholders to enforcement actions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds in two consecutive financial years: total balance sheet assets above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average workforce above 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 as amended, implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be applied where permitted and is mandatory for public-interest consolidated entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must provide an initial UBO declaration to the RBE within 1 month of incorporation and file any modification within 1 month of each change. Annually, the gérant must confirm that the recorded beneficial-ownership data remains accurate; the annual RBE confirmation is due by 31 March. Any share transfer that changes the beneficial owner must be reflected in the share register and filed with the RBE within 1 month of the transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book with General Meeting Minutes

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City): 17% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax on taxable base; rate varies by commune.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No traditional tax holidays apply to e-commerce; main incentives: (i) 100% participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains where participation is at least 10% (or acquisition cost at least EUR 1.2 million) for a 12-month holding period; (ii) 80% IP box exemption for qualifying intellectual property income, corresponding to an effective aggregate rate of about 4.99%; (iii) Luxembourg investment tax credit for qualifying digital capital equipment; (iv) loss carryforward limited by the compliance template to 5 years.
